subject: pe
title: Three Lever Classes
welcome_lead: 1st, 2nd, 3rd class — find the fulcrum in every joint.
meta_desc: A-Level PE adventure on lever systems in the human body.
final_note: Most human levers trade force for range and speed — efficient for movement, costly for strength.

concepts.def: Fulcrum between effort and load (e.g., head on atlas vertebra).
Load between fulcrum and effort (e.g., calf raise on ball of foot).
Effort between fulcrum and load (e.g., biceps curl) — most common in body.
Effort arm ÷ load arm; >1 amplifies force, <1 amplifies speed.
Pivot point of the lever (usually a joint).
Force × perpendicular distance to fulcrum (N m).

walkthroughs.body_html: Identify fulcrum, effort and load order. First-class is rare; third-class dominates.
MA = effort arm/load arm. Calf raise (MA>1) amplifies force; biceps curl (MA<1) amplifies speed.
Most joints favour wide range and fast movement — adaptive for hunting, throwing and locomotion.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between strength and power?
options: Strength is for the upper body, power for the lower.
Second class.
They are the same thing.
Strength is maximum force; power is force times speed of movement.
